title: The Stability Review opens with the five measures, per piece of work rather than per week
description:
## As asked

**Repository:** JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** We read five measures, in this order when they clash:

1. no new mess (ordinary tickets read neutral or better in a blind read);
2. the curve: net production lines, with deletions per addition, CI time, Waiting entries in the area notes, and tickets minted per landing beside it;
3. speed (time and sessions per ticket);
4. the person's seat (questions that were really theirs, and runs that needed no operator);
5. cost per finished task, measured but not optimised for now.

The Stability Review already runs as a Periodical. John: "weekly is sort of the wrong cadence as it's based on how much happened."

**What we want.** The Stability Review opens with those five measures in that order, each per landing or per task rather than per day or week, so a reading means the same however busy the period was. Net production lines lead, with code and comments counted apart, so we can see whether the share of comment-only lines falls. No new scheduling: the review runs as Periodicals already do.

**The starting point (8 November):**

* net source growth +1.56k lines a day (about 2,390 added, 830 deleted);
* 0.35 lines deleted per line added;
* production JavaScript 206,782 lines; by the area registry's count (207,338 lines), 82,154 are comment-only;
* CI median 8.55 minutes;
* 66 Waiting entries (56 Harbour, 10 runner);
* 1.43 tickets minted per landing;
* round 1 cost about $24 a ticket;
* one task (LIN-4393): 8 sessions, $14.94, 54 minutes from first Survey to merge.

**Done when** the next Stability Review opens with the five measures in order, per piece of work, with code and comments apart, set against the 8 November starting point.

**Every change names what it retires. Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself; only John's calls (product, money, authority, what to retire) go to him as rulings.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** consolidate the decision this task touches
**Why:** The review opens with all five measures per landing or task, fed by one committed, re-runnable measure sharing the registry's comment counter; without it each run rebuilds its counting and no reading compares with the starting point.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** the standing policy

## Implementation Plan

*Plan at* `30a019289` *(HEAD, 12 Nov). It builds on both Surveys (open-0 and global, 12 Nov) and the size record. Every figure below was re-measured at HEAD by this pass unless it is quoted from the ask.*

### What this is for, and what done looks like

The ask: the Stability Review "opens with those five measures in that order, each per landing or per task rather than per day or week, so a reading means the same however busy the period was. Net production lines lead, with code and comments counted apart." Done (the ticket's own Done-when): "the next Stability Review opens with the five measures in order, per piece of work, with code and comments apart, set against the 8 November starting point."

The ask is about ordering the prompt, but the real cause is somewhere else: **each run rebuilds its own measuring**. Run 5 copied and wrote five scripts into `docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-08-stability/` and still could not reproduce three of run 4's rows ("counting rule was not recovered"). The 8 November figures also use three definitions of "source". Changing the prompt's words cannot make two readings comparable. One committed, re-runnable measure can. So the change has two parts, and the measure comes first:

1. **One committed measure** that prints all five measures per landing or per finished task, in the ask's order, with the 8 November reference beside each row.
2. **A neutral clause in the shared Stability prompt**: if the repo declares its own measures, the review opens with them; otherwise it runs as it does now.

**Cuts to the** `## As asked` **block: none.** The one candidate cut, measures 1 and 4 printing "not measured", is already raised as ruling `lin4399-m1m4-placeholder`. It recommends building both, and its unanswered default is "build both; no cut is agreed". This plan builds both (P1.4 and P1.5) and does not raise the question again. If John answers `placeholder`, P1.4 and P1.5 shrink to a row that reads "not measured" with the reason; nothing else changes.

### Decisions

**D1. Where Harbour's measures live: in this repository, never in the shared prompt.** `generateStabilityReviewPrompt` (`lib/periodicals.js:589`) is rendered for every workspace. Harbour's measures, its paths and its 8 Nov numbers go in a declaration committed here, `docs/reviews/stability-measures/README.md`, with the reference output beside it. The prompt finds the declaration by searching the repo, the way Seams & Tangles finds its committed tool ("no path is written here"; `generateSeamsTanglesPrompt`). *Set aside:* writing the five measures into the template (it would give every workspace Harbour's review, and it breaks the rule that shared prompts name no paths, `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` Waiting, the `areaNotes()` entry from Drift & Coherence, 10 Nov). *Set aside:* a new Periodical (the ask says no new scheduling, and it would split one review into two).

**D2. One counter: the registry's Acorn counter, on the code-shape kit's Harbour scope.** "Net production lines" means the change in `shape-core.mjs` totals (`codeLines`, `commentLines`, `blankLines`) between the window's base and head. The scope is `^(server\.js$|(lib|routes|public)/.*\.[cm]?js$)` with the kit's default excludes. This reconciles the ask's three definitions, as checked at HEAD:

* At `9574d537` (run 5's pin) the kit reads **206,784** lines: 110,011 code, **82,161** comment-only, 14,612 blank. The ask quotes 206,782 (the regex counter) and 82,154 of 207,338 (the registry count). The comment-only figure is within 7 lines. The declaration records the residual gap and does not hide it.
* Over `5334c81a..9574d537` (114 first-parent landings), first-parent `--numstat --no-renames` on the same scope gives 10,235 added and 3,677 deleted. Net 6,558 equals the shape difference exactly (206,784 − 200,226). One definition therefore serves both the net figure and deletions per addition.
* Per landing: **+57.5 net** (code +26.6, comment-only +27.9, blank +3.0), 89.8 added, 32.3 deleted, **0.36** deleted per added. The comment-only share went from 39.4% to 39.7%. That is the signal the ask wants to see fall. Open-0's "+61 net / 93 added" used run 5's `src` bucket, a different scope; the declaration names both.

The script imports `scripts/code-shape/shape-core.mjs` and `code-shape-lib.mjs` (`git`, `listBlobs`, `readBlobs`, `compileScope`). It does not copy them. `scripts/steady-base-code.mjs` is untouched: papers cite it, and retiring it is John's call.

**D3. Per piece of work: the units.** The denominator is LinearViewer first-parent landings in the window. A measure that is a property of a task uses **finished tasks**: ticket ids named by the window's landings whose issue is Done with `completedAt` inside the window. A ticket landed in pieces therefore counts once, in the window where it finished. Ids that landed but are not yet finished are counted and printed, not dropped. A count measure (Waiting entries) is reported as its totals at both ends and the change per landing. A duration that is already per run (CI) is reported as the median over the window's main runs.

**D4. Sources outside this repo are named, never reached silently.** The registry row stays `scope: 'repo'`. The declaration states that the Harbour reading also uses (a) the workspace API proxy for tracker measures, (b) `gh` for CI, and (c) the runner checkout for its Waiting entries. Run 5 already read both repositories. Each source is an explicit input. A source that is absent or unreadable prints its row as `not measured: <reason>`, and a partial read prints how many items were unreadable. Nothing is zero-filled. This settles the brief's second open question without a workspace-scope home, which stays out of scope (global Survey).

**D5. Shape of the code: a pure core and a thin command-line wrapper.** The kit's own pattern (`*-core.mjs` plus a CLI).

* `scripts/stability-measures-core.mjs`: pure functions only. It takes numstat records, shape totals at two commits, Waiting counts, CI runs, per-task tracker records and blind-read signs, and returns the ordered reading. It does no I/O.
* `scripts/stability-measures.mjs <repo> <base> <head> [--runner <dir>] [--api <base>] [--blind <signs.json>]`: does the git, `gh` and proxy reads, and prints JSON on stdout plus a short ordered summary (the review's opening table) on stderr. `--api` defaults to `$HARBOUR_LOCAL_BASE/api/proxy`. Proxy reads honour 429 `Retry-After` (60/min).
* Tests live in `tests/unit/stability-measures.test.js`, which imports the core. 46 unit tests already import `scripts/`, so `package.json` and CLAUDE.md (11,994 of 12,000 bytes) do not change. The core is not put in `scripts/code-shape/`, because the kit's contract is "committed git objects only", and tracker and CI reads break it.

**D6. The neutral prompt clause (part 2).** One bullet is added to `generateStabilityReviewPrompt`, and one phrase is reworded. The bullet says: if the repo commits its own declaration of this review's measures (their definitions, order, unit of work, reference reading and the tool that measures them), the review task opens its report with those measures, in that order and that unit, each beside the reference reading, read with the committed tool. A measure the tool cannot read is printed as not measured, with the reason, never estimated. The trajectory assessment follows unchanged. With no declaration, the review runs as now. "introducing no new tooling" becomes "introducing no tooling beyond what the repo commits". "relative", "never absolute counts" and the trajectory framing stay, because the declared measures are normalised per unit of work, which is relative. *Set aside:* changing `cadence: 'weekly'` or adding a trigger on landings (the ask says no new scheduling; a trigger would need its own ruling). *Set aside:* touching Recent Headwinds' altitude text. Its hash stays, and Stability's opening is a reading, not headwind findings.

**D7. Registry placement.** The two new scripts get a narrow pattern, `^scripts/stability-measures(-core)?\.mjs$`, in Reports & operator tools (`docs/areas/areas.json`), following LIN-3829's retention precedent. No existing file is re-filed, so no census or co-change count moves (`docs/areas/README.md`, "The registry"). A placement test pins it: both files land in Reports & operator tools, and `scripts/steady-base-code.mjs` and `scripts/code-shape/verbatim.mjs` stay unmapped.

### The five measures (what the script prints, in this order)

Each row carries its definition key, its value for the window, and the 8 Nov reference (P1.7).

1. **No new mess.** The share of sampled ordinary landings whose blind read is neutral or better (better, neutral or mixed), the number read worse, and the mean sign (+1 better, 0 neutral or mixed, −1 worse, as in `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md`). *Ordinary* means a landing that names a ticket and touches something outside `docs/`. The sample is fixed by rule, not chosen: up to 8 landings, spaced evenly in landing order, so a re-run picks the same ones. Without `--blind` the script prints the sample and `pending blind reads`. The review run gives each sampled commit a fresh reader that sees only that commit's diff and the frozen prompt (`docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started-evidence/2026-11-06/prompts/blind-read-prompt.md`), records each Balance verbatim in `signs.json`, and re-runs with `--blind`. When LIN-4396 (blind read before merge, Backlog) lands, its recorded reads can replace the sample; the declaration says so.
2. **The curve.** Net production lines per landing, with code, comment-only and blank apart, and the comment-only share at base and head (leads the row). Added and deleted per landing, and deleted per added. CI median: successful `test.yml` main runs whose head sha is a window landing, `updatedAt − startedAt`, the same rule as run 5's `measure_ci.py`. Waiting entries: totals at base and head and the change per landing, for Harbour and the runner separately and summed. Tickets minted per landing, labelled **ID-span estimate**: the highest issue number created at or before the head's commit time, minus the same at the base, found by reading single issues' `createdAt` (the issue list has no timestamps). The span counts trashed ids.
   * A Waiting entry is a `- ` bullet under `## Waiting` in `docs/areas/*.md`, read from git objects. Checked at HEAD: this rule gives **56** at `9574d537` and **10** in the runner at `5d8489e` (run 5's runner pin), so the ask's 66 = 56 + 10 reproduces exactly. For the runner, the script uses the last commit on its checked-out branch at or before the base and head commit times.
3. **Speed.** Per finished task: the median and mean time from its first dispatch to its last landing, and the median and mean sessions. A session is a dispatch row that is not `kind: 'wake'`. Checked: LIN-4393 has 14 rows, 6 of them wakes, so 8 sessions, matching the ask.
4. **The person's seat.**
   * *Questions that were really theirs:* rulings raised per finished task, and the share the person answered rather than dismissed. A dismissed ruling was by definition not theirs.
   * *Runs that needed no operator:* the share of finished tasks with no ruling, no dispatch row that went `blocked` or was closed with `closedReason: 'operator'`, and no dispatch started by a person.
   * Two facts are unverified at HEAD, and the builder checks both first: whether `GET /rulings?issueIdentifier=…&includeResolved=true` returns a task's answered and dismissed rulings (the manual warns that task-bound rows are not covered), and whether `GET /dispatch/{id}` `dispatchedBy` tells a person from autopilot. If either is missing, that half prints `not measured: <the field that is missing>` and the plan records it in the PR. It does not guess.
5. **Cost per finished task.** The median and mean of `totalUsd` from `GET /issues/{id}/cost` (LIN-4393 reads $14.94, matching the ask), with any `unpriced` or `noTelemetryCount` totals shown. This is measured, not optimised.

### The pieces, in landing order

**Part 1: the measure (PR 1).**

* P1.1 The core and its tests (D5).
* P1.2 The command-line wrapper: git and shape reads (D2), Waiting (measure 2), CI through `gh`.
* P1.3 Tracker reads: finished tasks, speed, cost and minted.
* P1.4 The blind-read sample and its `--blind` tally.
* P1.5 The seat reads, after the two checks in measure 4.
* P1.6 The registry pattern and the placement test (D7).
* P1.7 The declaration `docs/reviews/stability-measures/README.md`: the five measures in order, each with its definition and source; the invocation; the D4 sources; the 8 Nov starting point quoted as the ask gives it, with its definitions (per day, run 5's `src` bucket, the regex counter); and the reconciliation in D2. Run the script on `5334c81a..9574d537` with `--runner` at the simple-dispatcher checkout and commit the output as `reference-2026-11-08.json`. The reference has no blind read or seat figures, because the 8 Nov starting point had none. Those rows say "no 8 Nov reading; the first reading sets it", and the 8 Nov paper's blind baseline is cited as a different method, not as a comparison.

**Part 2: the prompt (PR 2, after PR 1 is on main).**

* P2.1 The clause and rewording (D6) and the doc comment on `generateStabilityReviewPrompt`.
* P2.2 New tests in the Stability block of `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js` (witnesses below).
* P2.3 Re-pin `stability-review` only in `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js`, with a LIN-4399 paragraph in its header giving the reason and the byte growth. Periodical prompts have no size ceiling yet; the size entry in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` Waiting (Documentation Review, 10 Nov) is context, so keep the clause to one short bullet.

**Retires.**

* The practice of copying or writing measuring scripts into each run's evidence folder: the declaration says the review runs the committed script. Frozen evidence folders stay, because published reports cite them.
* The per-day rows of `project-velocity-trajectory` (LV and SD): the declaration tells the next report to close that ledger row as superseded by the opening measures, not to recompute it per day.
* The template's "introducing no new tooling".

### Every place the behaviour lives

The behaviour is "what the Stability Review measures, and in what unit". Search used: `grep -rli "stability review\|stability-review\|generateStabilityReviewPrompt"` over the repo, excluding `docs/reviews`, `docs/papers` and `experiments`.

* **In scope:** `lib/periodicals.js` (the prompt and its doc comment), `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`, `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js`, and the new declaration and scripts.
* **Out of scope, with reasons:**
  * `scripts/code-shape/README.md` says only that per-file churn belongs to Stability, which is still true.
  * `scripts/survey-hides-periodicals.mjs` is a one-off that names templates only.
  * Past `docs/reviews/stability-review-*.md` and their evidence are frozen records.
  * Recent Headwinds' text is covered in D6.
* **What no search reaches:** what the next live run actually writes. Part 2's witness is the next Stability Review report itself, which the Done-when names.

### Likeliest ways it breaks, and the witness for each behaviour

1. **The shared prompt leaks Harbour.** Witness: a Part 2 test that the Stability prompt names no repo path (`/\b(scripts|docs|lib)\//`), none of the 8 Nov numbers, and no `LIN-` id. Plus a test that it still tells a repo with no declaration to discover its own sources.
2. **The loosened guard.** "No new tooling" becomes "beyond what the repo commits". Witness: a test that the wording still forbids tooling the review run would write itself (it matches "beyond what the repo commits" and does not match the old unconditional ban). Plus the existing `relative` / `absolute` / `trajectory` tests, which stay green unchanged.
3. **The counting rule drifts from the registry's.** Witness: a core test on a tiny fixture (code, comment-only and blank lines, and a line with code and a trailing comment) giving the split that `shape-core` gives. And the committed reference reproduces D2's figures: 114 landings, net 6,558 = code +3,034, comment +3,185, blank +339; deleted per added 0.36; Waiting 0 → 56 and runner 10.
4. **Tracker reads undercount silently.** Witness: core tests where an unreadable cost, a 429 that never clears, or a missing ruling read is reported as unreadable with a count, never as zero. LIN-4393's 8 sessions and $14.94 come out of the core from a recorded fixture.
5. **The re-pin hides another template moving.** Witness: only `stability-review`'s two hashes change; the other 15 stay byte-identical.
6. **The placement pattern widens.** Witness: the placement test in D7.

### Area notes weighed

* `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`:
  * Lessons: prompt size is frozen. This binds stage prompts; Periodicals are pinned by hash only, so the re-pin carries the reason.
  * Waiting: the `areaNotes()` path-spelling entry (Drift & Coherence, 10 Nov) supports D1.
  * Waiting: the Periodical prompt ceiling entry (Documentation Review, 10 Nov) is context, not scope.
* `docs/areas/README.md`, "The registry": the LIN-3829 caution against `scripts/` patterns is met by the narrow pattern in D7.
* `docs/areas/reports-and-operator-tools.md`: nothing bears on this.
* **Files that keep changing:** the last 15 commits on `lib/periodicals.js` and its tests are LIN-4398, LIN-4390, LIN-4381, LIN-4380 and LIN-4379, all reshaping shared Periodical bullets and re-pinning hashes. Rebase before re-pinning, and recompute the hash on the rebased tree, never by hand.
* **Staleness:** those files have changed since the ticket was created (10 Nov). Everything here was read at `30a019289`.

### Session fit and review

needs multiple sessions. Concretely, one session would lose track of three data sources, each needing its own check (git and shape, `gh`, and the proxy, including two unverified fields), the reconciliation of the reference against the 8 Nov figures, and the shared-prompt re-pin. Split at the PR seam: Part 1 lands and is verified by its reference output; Part 2 lands on top and is verified by its tests and the next live review.

plan-review due: yes. It needs more than one session and loosens a guard in a shared prompt contract ("no new tooling").

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4399 @ 30a019289

**Why it will be hard**

1. **The ticket asks for a prompt change, but the real problem is the measuring tool.** Each review rebuilds its numbers by hand. Run 5 wrote its own scripts (`docs/reviews/_evidence-2026-11-08-stability/measure_*.py`) and still could not reproduce run 4 on three rows ("counting rule was not recovered"). Reordering the prompt won't make a reading "mean the same however busy the period was". A committed, re-runnable measure would.

2. **The baseline uses three definitions of "source".**
   - "Net source growth" is run 5's `src` bucket.
   - 206,782 matches the regex counter in `scripts/steady-base-code.mjs`.
   - 207,338 / 82,154 match the acorn counter behind the area registry (`scripts/code-shape/shape.mjs`).

   Splitting code from comments needs one counter. I'd pin the registry's, since the ask cites it.

3. **The baseline is per day; the target is per landing.** Run 5's delta window (114 landings, 10,635 added, 3,697 deleted) gives roughly **+61 net, 93 added per landing**. Some measures don't become a rate: Waiting entries are a count (report the change per landing). CI median and deletions per addition already fit.

4. **Two of the five measures have nothing to measure them.**
   - (1) Blind read: `docs/papers/harbour/cleaner-than-it-started.md` was a one-off study; the review has no step for it.
   - (4) The person's seat: I found no counter for either half.

   (3) and (5) can come from `GET /api/proxy/issues/{id}/cost` (`workerSessions`, with `costUsd` and `durationMs`). Minted per landing is an ID-span estimate, because the issue list has no timestamps.

5. **The template is generic, and pinned by tests.**
   - `generateStabilityReviewPrompt` (`lib/periodicals.js:589`) is repo-neutral ("discover what trajectory data is available rather than assuming a source"). Hardcoding Harbour's measures and baseline would give every workspace Harbour's review.
   - Its sha256 is pinned (`tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js:58`). Phrase tests (`tests/unit/periodicals.test.js:742`) require "relative" and "trajectory"; per-landing wording fits them.
   - Waiting and landings span both repos, but the template's scope is `'repo'`.

6. **Cadence is still `'weekly'`** (`lib/periodicals.js:1087`). The ask says no new scheduling, so this only changes the units. A trigger based on landings would be a separate ruling.

**What I'd do first**

Commit one script, `scripts/stability-measures.mjs <base> <head>`. It would print, per landing and in the ask's order:
- net production lines, with code and comment-only apart (registry counter);
- deletions per addition;
- CI median;
- change in Waiting entries;
- tickets minted;
- sessions, minutes and dollars per task.

Measures 1 and 4 would print **not yet measured** rather than be guessed. Run it on `5334c81a..9574d537` to restate the 8 November baseline per landing, and commit the output as the reference.

Then make the prompt general: open with the measures the repo declares, and use its script if one exists. The template stays neutral, Harbour's five measures stay in this repo, and the hash needs one re-pin.

**Retires:** the per-day velocity rows (`project-velocity-trajectory`) and the per-run copies of the measuring scripts.

**For John:** may measures 1 and 4 read "not measured" for now, or is building them in scope?

## Survey global: LIN-4399 @ 30a019289

**Where it lands.** In two places, and they are in different shape.

1. `lib/periodicals.js`: `generateStabilityReviewPrompt` and its registry row. Every workspace gets this shared prompt text. The area is well kept and being tidied right now (LIN-4379, LIN-4380, LIN-4390 and LIN-4398 this week), but it is growing. The llm-and-prompts note records Periodical prompts up 18.8% in its window, with the sha256 pin as the only check on size. The Stability text is essentially LIN-453's from June, and it now contradicts what is asked: "introducing no new tooling", "never absolute counts", sources it must find for itself, and `scope: 'repo'`.
2. `scripts/`: where measuring actually happens. It holds 236 files; since 1 Oct, 139 were added and 11 deleted. Most are one-offs tied to a single ticket (`steady-base-*`, `survey-check-*`, `lin-4200-*`, `delivery-composition.mjs`). There are already two counters for comment lines: the regex one in `scripts/steady-base-code.mjs` and the Acorn one in `scripts/code-shape/`. This part is getting worse, and it is the deeper symptom. Readings don't reproduce because each run rebuilds its own measuring tool.

**Done the obvious way.** Writing the five measures and the 8 Nov baseline into the template would put Harbour's own numbers into every workspace's prompt. It would also break the rule that shared prompts name no paths (see `areaNotes()`, and census-review's "no path is written here"), and make the prompt longer again. A `stability-measures.mjs` that counts lines itself would be a third comment counter and one more one-off. Measures 3–5 (sessions, cost, tickets minted, runs with no operator) come from the tracker and the workspace, not from repo history. Runner's Waiting entries are in another repo. Under `'repo'` scope, the script would either reach across repos without saying so or undercount.

These would have to learn about the change: the Stability block in `tests/unit/periodicals.test.js`, and the hash pin in `tests/unit/lin-4313-periodical-prompt-bytes.test.js`. The pin is the only thing that would notice. The registry in `docs/areas/areas.json` lists a few scripts by name, so a new script has no area until it gets a pattern. Reports & operator tools already holds `pipeline-churn.mjs` and the code-shape retention scripts.

**Better, at a cost this task can carry.**
- Template: add one neutral clause. If the repo declares its own measures (definitions, order, reference reading, script), open with them per landing or task, then give the trajectory read. Otherwise run as now. Reword "no new tooling" to "no tooling beyond what the repo commits", and re-pin the hash on purpose.
- One script that imports the code-shape Acorn counter rather than copying it, with its definitions and the 8 Nov reference output committed beside it. It retires the per-run Stability measurement scripts. Leave `steady-base-code.mjs` alone: papers under `docs/papers/harbour/` cite it, so retiring it is John's call.
- Print "not measured" for measures 1 and 4 rather than guessing. Label tickets-minted-per-landing as an estimate from the span of issue IDs.
- Give the script a pattern in the registry in the same change.

**Better still, not this task's to carry.** A lifecycle for `scripts/`, so one-offs retire when their ticket closes. A size limit for Periodical prompts. Timestamps on the proxy's issue list, so tickets minted stops being an estimate. A home at workspace scope for measures that span repos.

## Plan written: LIN-4399 @ 30a019289

The plan is in the description under `## Implementation Plan`. In short:

- **Two PRs.** First, one committed measure (`scripts/stability-measures.mjs` and its pure core), with Harbour's declaration and the 8 Nov reference under `docs/reviews/stability-measures/`. Second, a neutral clause in the shared Stability prompt that opens with any measures a repo declares, and a re-pin of `stability-review`'s hash only.
- **One counter: the registry's Acorn one.** On `5334c81a..9574d537` it gives +57.5 net lines per landing (code +26.6, comment-only +27.9, blank +3.0) and 0.36 lines deleted per line added. The comment-only share rose from 39.4% to 39.7%. At `9574d537` it reads 82,161 comment-only lines, against the 82,154 the ask quotes.
- **The Waiting rule reproduces the ask's 66** (56 Harbour + 10 runner). LIN-4393's 8 sessions and $14.94 come straight from the dispatch history and `/cost`.
- **Cuts: none.** Measures 1 and 4 are built, following the open ruling `lin4399-m1m4-placeholder` (if unanswered: build both). I have not raised it again.

### Plan Review Verdict

**Verdict:** Approve. The plan's premise holds: readings don't compare because each run rebuilds its own measuring. Every figure it stands on reproduces at `30a019289`, and the two-PR order fits the work.

**How it meets what was asked.** The ask is "opens with those five measures in that order, each per landing or per task … Net production lines lead, with code and comments counted apart … No new scheduling". The plan delivers all five, in order, per landing or per finished task, set against the 8 Nov starting point, with cadence and scheduling untouched. It makes no cuts.
